$comment: Optional MCP servers for this plugin. They are NOT in .mcp.json because each
one needs an endpoint or command that only the operator can supply, and a
server that fails to start is worse than one that was never declared.
To enable a server: copy its entry into .mcp.json, replace the placeholder
command or URL with the one your organisation runs, and export the listed
environment variables in your shell or secret manager.
Never put a token value in this file or in .mcp.json. Use ${VAR} references
only. These files are committed to a repository.

local-otel-tools.$comment: A local HTTP MCP server exposing OpenTelemetry audit and verify tools — the loop that reads a collector config or SDK setup and reports what it would actually emit. Enable it if your team runs one; the skills work without it. Adjust the port to match your server.

splunk-observability.$comment: Splunk Observability Cloud: verify a MetricSet exists, read APM workflows and Tag Spotlight cardinality, and check whether an attribute actually landed as a dimension. Used by instrumentation-analyze for the existing-footprint inventory and by instrumentation-guide for portfolio-verifiable exit criteria.
splunk-observability.command: <command your org runs for the Splunk Observability MCP server>

splunk-platform.$comment: Splunk Enterprise or Cloud Platform: run the SPL behind a Log Observer Connect panel, and confirm trace_id is indexed on the events a dashboard joins to. Used when the guide specifies the LOC panel shape.
splunk-platform.command: <command your org runs for the Splunk platform MCP server>

thousandeyes.$comment: Cisco ThousandEyes: list existing tests and agent locations so the guide recommends path coverage for hops that are genuinely unmonitored rather than duplicating a test that already exists.
thousandeyes.command: <command your org runs for the ThousandEyes MCP server>
